title: Coordinate Plane Basics Practice
description: Practice identifying axes, origin, quadrants, and ordered pairs.

questions.question: Which axis is horizontal on a coordinate plane?
questions.explanation: The x-axis is the horizontal number line. The y-axis is vertical.

questions.question: What is the origin written as an ordered pair?
questions.explanation: The origin is where the x-axis and y-axis meet, so both coordinates are 0.

questions.question: In the ordered pair (6, -2), the x-coordinate is 6.
questions.explanation: The x-coordinate is the first number in an ordered pair.

questions.question: Which movement matches the point (-3, 4)?
questions.explanation: A negative x-coordinate means left, and a positive y-coordinate means up.

questions.question: Which quadrant contains the point (5, -7)?
questions.explanation: The signs (+, -) place the point in Quadrant IV.

questions.question: Write the ordered pair for a point 2 units right and 5 units down from the origin.
questions.explanation: Right gives a positive x-coordinate, and down gives a negative y-coordinate, so the ordered pair is (2, -5).

questions.question: Where is the point (0, -6) located?
questions.explanation: When x = 0, the point lies on the y-axis. Axis points are not in quadrants.

questions.question: In one sentence, explain why (4, 3) and (3, 4) are different points.
questions.correctAnswer: The order matters because (4, 3) means 4 right and 3 up, while (3, 4) means 3 right and 4 up.
questions.explanation: Ordered pairs are read as (x, y), so switching the numbers changes the horizontal and vertical movements.
